input.title: Red Willow Ranch
input.premise: A warm slice-of-life story at a modest fictional prairie cattle ranch. Alex and Erin Morrow share a small farmhouse, twelve beef cows and two leisure riding horses, Clover and Pippin. Ben helps a few mornings a week; their neighbor June is a friend. A morning can include loading supplementary feed in the shed, driving it to the cows, making breakfast, grooming a horse or choosing a quiet ride. Other days leave room for the garden, laundry, small repairs, baking and neighborly tea. Begin at the farmhouse kitchen table after overnight drizzle, before the feeding round. Let relationships and everyday physical actions shape the story; no forced crisis or required sequence of chores.
input.narrationStyle: Warm, grounded slice-of-life prose. Close third-person human viewpoint, tactile rural detail, natural dialogue and gentle humour. Give small practical actions room without turning each passage into a task list.
input.artStyle: Natural-light rural photography, realistic materials and colours, calm compositions, soft prairie daylight.

preferences.writingGuide: Stay with one human viewpoint per passage. Let each scene do one manageable thing and stop at the requested boundary. Show travel, boarding, exits and handovers when they occur. Use exact whole units for tracked transfers or consumption; do not guess numerical capacity from vague words. Background routines describe possibilities, not completed events. Allow conversation, rest and unfinished chores.
preferences.contentNotes: Adult human cast; family-friendly domestic and farm life. Affection is welcome. No explicit sexual content, cruelty or forced catastrophe.

places.name: Red Willow Ranch
places.description: A small family-run prairie cattle ranch. Farm Yard links the farmhouse, Feed Shed, horse areas and pasture gates; Farm Lane joins the county road.
places.visualDescription: Gently rolling grassland, shelterbelt trees, gravel tracks and weathered red outbuildings.

places.name: Small Farmhouse
places.description: A modest one-storey home with a kitchen, sitting room, two bedrooms, bathroom and a back mudroom opening toward Farm Yard.
places.visualDescription: Cream clapboard, green trim, a low shingled roof and a covered front porch.

places.name: Farmhouse Kitchen
places.description: A lived-in kitchen for breakfast, baking and planning the day. Kitchen Table, Refrigerator and Pantry Cupboard hold the named household supplies.
places.visualDescription: Pale yellow walls, pine cabinets, a blue checked tablecloth and an east window over the sink.

places.name: Sitting Room
places.description: A comfortable room for reading, conversation, mending and resting after chores; reached from the kitchen.
places.visualDescription: Faded green sofa, low bookshelf, braided rug and a broad west window.

places.name: Main Bedroom
places.description: Alex and Erin share this bedroom; clothes and ordinary personal belongings are kept here.
places.visualDescription: Patchwork quilt, pine chest of drawers and simple bedside lamps.

places.name: Spare Bedroom
places.description: A tidy guest room that also serves as a small sewing and paperwork space.
places.visualDescription: Single bed, sewing desk, gingham curtains and a folded guest quilt.

places.name: Farmhouse Bathroom
places.description: An ordinary bathroom for washing up after work and getting ready for the day.
places.visualDescription: White tub, sage-painted cabinet, tiled floor and a small frosted window.

places.name: Back Mudroom
places.description: The practical entrance between the kitchen and Farm Yard, with space for muddy boots, coats and a laundry basket.
places.visualDescription: Boot bench, wall pegs, rubber floor mat and a back door with a glass pane.

places.name: Front Porch
places.description: A sheltered place for tea, watching the weather and receiving visitors; steps lead toward Kitchen Garden and Farm Lane.
places.visualDescription: Two wooden chairs, narrow porch boards and a low painted railing.

places.name: Farm Yard
places.description: The gravel working hub. Feed Shed stands west, Workshop south, North Pasture gate north and Horse Yard east. There is space to park farm machinery.
places.visualDescription: Compacted gravel, shallow rain-dark patches and open space between low farm buildings.

places.name: Feed Shed
places.description: Dry livestock-feed storage with separate named stock containers. Farm machinery can be loaded outside its broad doors; the specific stock and tools are catalogued separately.
places.visualDescription: Red plank walls, wide sliding doors, timber rafters and a dry concrete floor.

places.name: Workshop
places.description: A small repair shop with a workbench and Workshop Toolbox. Suitable for minor repairs and sharpening tools.
places.visualDescription: Corrugated metal walls, scarred workbench, pegboard and a fluorescent strip light.

places.name: Loader Tractor
places.description: An operable compact loader tractor, represented as a moving place. Tractor Cab is inside it; Tractor Feed Bin is attached outside. It can travel between Farm Yard, Feed Shed and North Pasture.
places.visualDescription: Faded green bodywork, black rubber tyres, orange beacon and a square glazed cab.

places.name: Tractor Cab
places.description: One driving seat, steering wheel and controls inside Loader Tractor. A driver stays in this cab while the tractor moves, and leaves it when stepping down.
places.visualDescription: Scuffed black seat, dusty glass, worn steering wheel and a small rear-view mirror.

places.name: North Pasture
places.description: A fenced grazing field north of Farm Yard. Cattle Feed Trough stands beside the accessible feeding strip, with Pasture Water Trough nearby. The herd can approach the trough.
places.visualDescription: Short autumn grass, wire fencing, a wide gate and a shallow rise backed by willow trees.

places.name: South Hay Meadow
places.description: A quiet grass field south of the yard, already cut for the season. Suitable for a boundary walk or an easy ride when the ground is firm.
places.visualDescription: Pale stubble, grass margins, a low stone pile and an open southern horizon.

places.name: Horse Yard
places.description: A separate area east of Farm Yard connecting Small Stable, Horse Paddock and Schooling Ring. Gates lead out toward Creek Loop Trail.
places.visualDescription: Packed earth, timber rails and a pair of neatly hung gate chains.

places.name: Small Stable
places.description: A two-stall stable used for the riding horses, shelter and grooming; the aisle connects Tack Room and both stalls.
places.visualDescription: Weathered red siding, dark green doors and a low roof with a ventilation cupola.

places.name: Stable Aisle
places.description: A broad, uncluttered aisle where the horses can be brought in for grooming or tacking up. Hooks provide storage for feed buckets when not in use.
places.visualDescription: Swept concrete, straw near stall doors and brass hooks along a timber wall.

places.name: Tack Room
places.description: Dry storage for Grooming Kit, saddles, bridles, halters and riding helmets. Tack is put away here when not being used.
places.visualDescription: Wooden saddle racks, bridle pegs, a narrow bench and a high dusty window.

places.name: Clover Stall
places.description: A bedded stall reserved for Clover, used when shelter or indoor care is wanted.
places.visualDescription: Fresh straw, a half-height wooden door and a small barred window.

places.name: Pippin Stall
places.description: A bedded stall reserved for Pippin, used when shelter or indoor care is wanted.
places.visualDescription: Clean straw, a broad stable door and a wall-mounted tie ring.

places.name: Horse Paddock
places.description: A secure turnout paddock for Clover and Pippin with grass, shade and Horse Water Trough. A gate opens into Horse Yard.
places.visualDescription: Timber rails, cropped grass, two shade trees and a muddy patch beside the gate.

places.name: Schooling Ring
places.description: A small enclosed sand arena for leisurely schooling and rebuilding confidence; it is not a competition yard.
places.visualDescription: Pale sand, low timber rails and two simple ground poles.

places.name: Kitchen Garden
places.description: A small garden beside the farmhouse, with late carrots, herbs and an unfinished herb-bed edging project. Garden Basket holds the small tools.
places.visualDescription: Raised beds, dark soil, rosemary pots and a low woven fence.

places.name: Creek Loop Trail
places.description: A gentle loop along the shelterbelt and creek, reached through the eastern horse gates or a southern grass track. Ordinary rides take time and return by the same gates.
places.visualDescription: Willow shade, a shallow creek, grass tracks and a small wooden footbridge beside the riding ford.

places.name: Farm Lane
places.description: A short gravel lane from Farm Yard past Front Porch to County Road. Walking to the neighboring smallholding takes about fifteen minutes.
places.visualDescription: Twin wheel tracks, grass verge, mailbox and a simple ranch sign.

places.name: County Road
places.description: A quiet public gravel road connecting the ranch lane and June Smallholding. Larger shops are a drive away and are not part of the starting scene.
places.visualDescription: Wide gravel shoulder, utility poles and open fields.

places.name: June Smallholding
places.description: June lives at this neighboring property beside County Road. A modest house and vegetable patch; visitors must travel here or arrange a visit.
places.visualDescription: White cottage, blue gate, tall sunflowers and a gravel front path.

relationships.notes: Married partners, affectionate and comfortable together; they share decisions and divide chores without keeping score.
A patient employer and mentor; trusts Ben with familiar jobs and explains unfamiliar machinery.
Friendly working relationship; enjoys helping him build confidence around the horses.
Friends who trade garden cuttings and sometimes plan an easy weekend ride.
Longstanding neighbors, comfortable sharing tea and practical help.
Erin is Clover's familiar rider and handler; their trust is expressed through ordinary horse behaviour.
Alex is Pippin's familiar rider; neither horse is a possession represented by an item record.

threads.title: A small latch adjustment
threads.notes: The pasture gate closes, but its catch is awkward. A minor repair can be fitted into a calm day; nothing has broken loose.

threads.title: An easy ride together
threads.notes: Erin would like an unhurried creek-loop ride when the ground dries. June could be invited, but no invitation or arrangement has happened.

threads.title: Finishing the herb bed
threads.notes: A little edging remains to be chosen for the kitchen garden. Alex and Erin have different ideas and can enjoy working it out.

canon.cargoNotes: Shared household operating money is 1,500 local dollars. Equipment is household property; item holder/storage records track physical custody, not legal title. No freight or deliveries are currently pending.

sceneBrief.purpose: Open with Alex and Erin at the kitchen table after light overnight rain. Let a warm breakfast conversation reveal their relationship and leave room to choose one next activity.
sceneBrief.tension: Only the ordinary pull between useful chores and making time for a pleasant day together.
sceneBrief.stopAt: End in the kitchen after a small choice or suggestion, before anyone starts or completes the outdoor chores.

lore.title: The scale of the day
lore.text: Present-day fictional prairie country, early autumn. Overnight drizzle has passed; the morning is cool and brightening. This is a modest ranch with twelve cows and two leisure riding horses, not a large commercial operation. Ordinary meals, chores, conversations and rest are worthwhile scenes. There is no predetermined crisis or hidden mystery.

lore.title: The cattle feeding round
lore.text: Supplementary cattle feeding uses Cattle Feed from Grain Hopper in Feed Shed. Whole scoops can be loaded into Tractor Feed Bin on Loader Tractor, driven to North Pasture and poured into Cattle Feed Trough. Tractor Cab is inside the tractor. Choose and state any moved whole-scoop count; loading and pouring are transfers, while actual eating consumes feed. This is a possible routine, not an event already completed.

lore.title: Preparing the horses' feed
lore.text: Horse Pellets are in Horse Feed Bin and Hay Flakes in Hay Rack, both in Feed Shed. Clover Feed Bucket and Pippin Feed Bucket start in Stable Aisle. Feed can be carried to the horses or the horses brought in from Horse Paddock. Keep moved whole scoops and hay flakes explicit; no nutritional calculation is required.

lore.title: An unhurried grooming session
lore.text: Grooming Kit in Tack Room contains Wooden Grooming Brush, Curry Comb and Hoof Pick. Clover and Pippin start in Horse Paddock; they can be brought to Stable Aisle. Taking a brush out, handing it over and putting it away are separate physical actions. The person holding a tool need not be its legal owner.

lore.title: Preparing a leisure ride
lore.text: Clover uses Clover Halter and Lead, Clover Trail Saddle and Clover Bridle; Pippin uses Pippin Halter and Lead, Pippin Riding Saddle and Pippin Bridle. Charcoal Riding Helmet and Green Riding Helmet are available. The equipment is put away in Tack Room after use. Horse Paddock, Stable Aisle and Creek Loop Trail provide turnout, preparation and a gentle outing. Riding moves each rider and horse to the same destination; horses remain characters, not moving rooms.

lore.title: A simple kitchen breakfast
lore.text: Kitchen Table holds Alex Blue Mug, Erin Cream Mug and Household Notebook. Refrigerator holds Eggs; Pantry Cupboard holds Bread Slices. Kitchen Kettle and Recipe Book are nearby. Tap water, tea and basic staples are ordinary background. Count only explicitly tracked whole eggs or slices used, rather than inventing a complete ingredient ledger.

lore.title: Adjusting the pasture latch
lore.text: North Pasture Gate closes securely but its latch catches. Adjustable Spanner in Workshop Toolbox at Workshop is available for a small adjustment. A repair is optional; this is not an escaped-cattle emergency.

lore.title: Time around the house
lore.text: Kitchen Garden has a small unfinished herb bed. Garden Basket there contains Garden Trowel and Gardening Gloves. Front Porch is pleasant for tea; Sitting Room has Evening Reading Book. Laundry Basket waits in Back Mudroom. These are alternatives for a quiet afternoon, not a compulsory checklist.

lore.title: Neighborly visits
lore.text: June Calloway starts at June Smallholding, a fifteen-minute walk from the farmhouse by Farm Lane and County Road. She can visit or be invited for tea and a future ride, but mentioning her does not make her arrive. No visit is arranged at the opening.

rules.text: Animals behave as ordinary animals and do not speak human dialogue. Keep narrative viewpoint with an adult human unless the user explicitly changes the story style.

Loader Tractor is a moving place with Tractor Cab inside it; Tractor Feed Bin is an item container attached to the tractor. Driving moves the tractor place; the driver stays in the cab until exiting. Do not create a duplicate tractor item.
